consumers.evidence: SimulationInput models new-store greenfield projections only; the single entry point is SiteEconomicsSimulator.simulate(SimulationInput). No ConversionSimulationInput or brownfield cash flow path exists: grep -n -i -E 'downtime|conversion|brownfield|remodel' modules/site_economics/domain/simulator.py at HEAD 944f4d71 (blob 30844af0), UTC 2026-09-08T17:57:12Z, raw exit 1, zero matches. Correction to an earlier over-broad claim: equipment residual value and salvage ARE already modelled for new-store assets via format_spec.residual_spec and machine_mix (raw exit 0, lines 325-356 and 529-531). What is missing is the brownfield use of residual value for OLD-format assets, so Stage B extends the existing residual path rather than creating one. See implementation-handoff.md section 5.3 Observation B.
consumers.stage_b_action: Extend simulator.py with ConversionSimulationInput: downtime loss = daily_baseline × downtime_days; net capex = remodeling_capex - residual_value + disposal_cost; apply conversion ramp curve.
acceptance_tests: Downtime is isolated: for one conversion scenario with every other financial input held fixed (remodeling_capex, residual_value, disposal_cost, ramp_months, ramp_curve_id, daily_baseline_revenue, target format, area), increasing downtime_days must strictly lower first-year net cash flow and must not shorten payback. This deliberately does NOT require a brownfield conversion to be worse than a greenfield baseline: different capex, residual and ramp inputs can outweigh downtime, so such a cross-scenario assertion would reject economically correct conversions.
Residual value increase causes proportional net capex decrease
Event replay with same event_id does not duplicate cost entries
Distinct events (different event_id) that both carry a null or omitted idempotency_key remain distinct and retain both cost entries; only a shared valid non-null key may collapse them

consumers.evidence: SiteScoreFeatureInput carries target_format_code (L70, the greenfield target format for a candidate site) but no conversion, brownfield, from_format, downtime or brand_transfer field: grep -n -i -E 'conversion|brownfield|from_format|downtime|remodel|brand_transfer' modules/sitescore/domain/scoring.py at HEAD 944f4d71 (blob 1f8f50ab), UTC 2026-09-08T17:57:28Z, raw exit 1, zero matches. SiteScore scores greenfield candidates against a single target format and consumes no conversion data. See implementation-handoff.md section 5.3 Observation C.
consumers.stage_b_action: TBD — depends on whether SiteScore should evaluate existing-store conversion ROI or only greenfield site selection. Requires product decision.
